solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Praise English girl about possessing mostly sound reasoning

indicators.note: the rearranged girl's name possesses, i.e. holds within it, the next piece
about here means the girl's name is moved around, its letters rearranged

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name

indicators.note: mostly means the word for sound reasoning loses its final letter

parts.note: logic is sound reasoning

explanation.surface: Someone compliments an English girl on the fact that her arguments are largely well reasoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' here rearranges the girl's name rather than meaning 'concerning'; 'possessing' then wraps it round the shortened reasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: To eulogise is to praise highly, typically in a formal speech or tribute.

clue.text: Chemical compound given which India, in a way, protested

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to sit in is one way of protesting, so in a way protested means sat in

explanation.surface: A chemical compound gets named after a nation's protest, as if India staged a sit-in.
explanation.walkthrough: A sit-in is a form of protest, so 'protested, in a way' gives SAT IN after I for India; 'given which' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: Isatin is an orange-red organic compound used in making dyes, derived from indigo.

clue.text: Put out note, following journalist

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
ff. is the abbreviation for following pages
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's standard journalist

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed by a note that came after a journalist's piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ff.' is the reference-book abbreviation for 'and the following pages'.
explanation.definitionFit: Put out is an adjective here meaning annoyed or offended, as is miffed.

clue.text: Plain gold currency's unknown

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
the dinar is the currency of several countries, such as Serbia and Jordan
y is a standard algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A puzzle about the value of a plain gold coin whose currency is a mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary and plain are synonyms for something unremarkable, without decoration.

clue.text: Forest member in promoted club

parts.note: rose means went up, as a promoted team does
a wood is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A Nottingham Forest player is now at a club that has just won promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: Nottingham Forest is an English football club, which the surface leans on; a tree is a member of a forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosewood is a tropical tree, so it is one of the many trees making up a forest.

clue.text: Drop this month's import licences initially

parts.note: inst., short for instant, is an old business abbreviation for this month

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letters of the words import and licences

explanation.surface: An instruction to abandon this month's import licences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inst.' (instant) in old business letters means 'of this month'.
explanation.definitionFit: Instil originally means to put in drop by drop, so it can stand for drop in that sense.

clue.text: Oat mixture 60% emulsified in a blender

indicators.note: put in a blender, the letters are mixed up into a new order
sixty per cent of a ten-letter word is its first six letters

explanation.surface: A breakfast mix of oats, more than half of it emulsified by a kitchen blender.
explanation.walkthrough: '60%' takes EMULSI, the first six of the ten letters of EMULSIFIED; 'in a blender' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a breakfast cereal of rolled oats mixed with dried fruit and nuts.

clue.text: Posh luxury car getting well across border

indicators.note: across says the word for well stretches across the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: sound means healthy or well
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
RR is short for Rolls-Royce

explanation.surface: A posh luxury car makes it safely over a national border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posh' gives U as in 'U and non-U', the old British upper-class label; 'getting' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A surround is a border or edging framing something, such as a fireplace.

clue.text: Automotive seller flopped badly

indicators.note: badly means the letters of seller flopped are rearranged

explanation.surface: A car dealer has failed miserably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges SELLER FLOPPED.
explanation.definitionFit: Automotive literally means moving under its own power, which is the meaning of self-propelled.

clue.text: Fresh new tofu intermittently lousy — hard on the inside

indicators.note: on the inside means the H goes within the rearranged letters
new means the pooled letters are made into a fresh arrangement
intermittently takes every other letter of the word lousy, starting with the first

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A food review: the new tofu is patchy and awful, with a tough centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intermittently' picks the odd letters of LOUSY, and 'new' shuffles them with the tofu before the H goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh and youthful both describe having the vigour or appearance of youth.

clue.text: Imagine lunch including fish? Au contraire

indicators.note: including says one piece holds another inside it
Au contraire, French for on the contrary, swaps the roles so the fish holds the lunch

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword regular
to lunch is to eat

explanation.surface: Picture a lunch with fish on the menu, or rather, the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Au contraire' flips 'including': the fish holds the lunch, not the lunch the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To ideate is to form an idea of something, to imagine or conceive it.

clue.text: Enlisted externally paid genius for organisation

indicators.note: for organisation means the letters are to be organised into a new order
externally means taking only the outside letters of the word paid

explanation.surface: A brilliant mind is paid from outside to work for an organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'externally' gives PD from PAID; 'for organisation' rearranges PD plus GENIUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Signed up and enlisted both mean joined, especially joined the armed forces.

clue.text: Fee to occupy vacated Azores Islands

indicators.note: to occupy means the fee sits inside the emptied word
vacated means emptied, leaving just the outside letters of Azores

parts.note: a toll is a fee for using a road or bridge

explanation.surface: A fee is charged to take over the abandoned Azores Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacated' empties Azores of its middle letters, leaving only its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Atolls are ring-shaped coral islands enclosing a lagoon.

clue.text: Times blocking offensive words

indicators.note: blocking means the times sign sits in the middle of the other word, blocking it

parts.note: the Tet Offensive was a 1968 campaign in the Vietnam War
x is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A newspaper censors offensive language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocking' puts X inside TET; 'Times' suggests the newspaper but is the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A text is a body of written words, as in the text of a speech.

clue.text: Man reportedly resisted university in a faraway place

parts.note: Tim is a man's name

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: bucked means resisted, as in bucking a trend

explanation.surface: A man apparently refused to go to university and ended up somewhere remote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' says the second part, 'bucked', is as heard: TIM plus BUKT, then U, sounds like 'Tim bucked U'.
explanation.definitionFit: Timbuktu, a town in Mali, is used proverbially for any remote, far-flung location.

clue.text: Suffering such aunts and uncles?

definitions.meaning: advice columnists who answer readers' problems are ... aunts and ... uncles

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether their aunts and uncles are a torment.
explanation.walkthrough: An agony aunt is a columnist who answers readers' personal problems.
explanation.definitionFit: Agony is extreme physical or mental suffering, and it is also the label for problem-page columnists.

clue.text: Jailhouse Rock

definitions.meaning: a prison, here the former federal prison in San Francisco Bay
The Rock is the nickname of the island prison

explanation.surface: The title of the Elvis Presley song Jailhouse Rock.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is the Elvis song title, split into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcatraz was a notorious federal penitentiary on an island known as The Rock.

clue.text: Fuel somewhat undervalued

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the word undervalued is used

explanation.surface: Fuel is a bit cheap for its worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' takes a run of letters from inside UNDERVALUED.
explanation.definitionFit: Derv is the British name for diesel fuel for road vehicles.

clue.text: Boy, keen to go outside, pulled up seaweed etc

indicators.note: pulled up, in a down clue, means the whole is read from bottom to top
to go outside means the word for keen goes around the boy

parts.note: eager means keen
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy eager to play outdoors yanks up seaweed and similar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go outside' gives EAGLADER; 'pulled up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Red algae are a large group of mostly marine algae, including many seaweeds, hence the etc.

clue.text: Deserted fancifully before introductions in Made In Chelsea

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before

indicators.note: introductions means the first letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone left in a fanciful way before appearing on the reality TV show Made in Chelsea.
explanation.walkthrough: Made in Chelsea is a British reality TV show about wealthy young Londoners. 'Deserted fancifully' reads 'deserted' as 'desert-ish'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eremic is an adjective meaning of or living in deserts, a playful reading of deserted.

clue.text: Protection against animal, boar or otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means the letters of boar or are put a different way

explanation.surface: A shield that guards against an animal, whether a boar or something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges BOAR OR. A roo is an Australian kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: A roo bar is a metal grille on a vehicle's front to protect it from collisions with kangaroos.

clue.text: European group of stars entertaining large paradisical location

indicators.note: entertaining means holding the next piece as a guest inside

parts.note: Dorado is a southern constellation
L is the clothing abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A European constellation plays host to a vast heavenly place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' puts L inside E plus DORADO, just after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: El Dorado was the legendary city of gold, now any place of fabulous wealth or paradise.

clue.text: Want to be part of avant-garde art history

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone aspires to belong to the history of avant-garde art.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave 'Want to be' as the definition, but 'to be' is a link word: 'Want' is the noun meaning lack, which DEARTH replaces.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a scarcity or lack, which is the noun sense of want.

clue.text: Drink up, fine beast

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means reading the word from the bottom upwards

parts.note: beer is a drink
OK means fine

explanation.surface: Someone says drink up, it's fine, beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses BEER.
explanation.definitionFit: The reebok, or rhebok, is a South African antelope, an animal.

clue.text: Take our money? Time to be strong

parts.note: to take our money is to rob us

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to take our money and says it is time to stay firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: Robust means sturdy and strong in constitution or structure.

clue.text: Poor girl left heart in Wales, coming back here?

indicators.note: coming back means the whole string is read in reverse order

parts.note: ill means poor, as in poor health
Ena is a girl's name

indicators.note: heart in means the central letter of the word Wales

explanation.surface: A sickly girl left her heart in Wales; will she return to this place?
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart in' gives L, the middle letter of WALES; 'coming back' reverses ILLENALL. The clue as a whole points to a Welsh town.
explanation.definitionFit: Llanelli is a town in South Wales, the place the clue's 'here' points to.

clue.text: Fantastic award set in motion for Asia?

definitions.note: an adverb sense, travelling in the direction of Asia

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly altered, so the letters of award set are reordered

explanation.surface: A wonderful prize is launched for Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fantastic' rearranges AWARD SET.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia lies east of Europe, so heading east is the direction of travel towards it.

clue.text: Trunk call reservation initially covered by levy

indicators.note: covered by means the call and letter sit inside the word for levy

parts.note: a tax is a levy
ho is a call to attract attention

indicators.note: initially means just the first letter of reservation

explanation.surface: A long-distance trunk call booking is subject to a charge.
explanation.walkthrough: A trunk call is the old British term for a long-distance phone call; here 'Trunk' is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The thorax is the chest region of the body, which is also called the trunk.
